title: systemd input segfaults (Probably caused by introduction of zstd?)
body:
## Bug Report

**Describe the bug**

I upgraded from `fluent-bit-3.2.6` to `fluent-bit-3.2.8` and `fluent-bit` started segfaulting.
The same upgrade also updated systemd from `257.2 -> 257.3`.

My theory is the following. But I don't know enough about `fluent-bit`'s build system to know if this is indeed the cause:

* `fluent-bit-3.2.7`  adds support for `zstd`. Statically linking against `zstd-1.5.6` https://github.com/fluent/fluent-bit/pull/9890
* `fluent-bit-3.2.8` bumps to `zstd-1.5.7` https://github.com/fluent/fluent-bit/pull/10021
* `libsystemd-257.3` dynamically links against `zstd-1.5.6` and `fluent-bit-3.2.8` dynamically links against `libsystemd-257.3`
* fluent-bit is somehow re-exporting the symbols from statically linked `zstd-1.5.7` so  `libsystemd`'s `sd_journal_enumerate_data` calls out to fluen-bits  statically-linked `zstd-1.5.7` whilst it expects `zstd-1.5.6`.  
* `ZSTD_freeDCtx` segfaults due to some ABI incompatibiltiy.

comments.body:
We have found the issue and unfortunately it's not a NixOS problem. NixOS compiles `libzstd` with `-DZSTD_LEGACY_SUPPORT=0` whilst Fedora and fluent-bit use the default of `-DZSTD_LEGACY_SUPPORT=5`. This means that the `ZSTD_DCtx` type is 16 bytes smaller (and has different field offsets) which causes fluent-bit to write data past the end of the allocation which subsequently causes `free()` to crash. The underlying symbol table pollution—the actual root cause—can be demonstrated on Fedora.  Thanks a lot to @participant5  for helping me dig into this.

Details:

Below is a `gdb` session demonstrating the cause of the issue on Fedora 41 using the binary provided by https://<redacted-host>/manual/installation/linux/redhat-centos

As you can see in the backtrace:

`decompress_blob_zstd` in `libsystemd` calls into `ZSTD_getFrameContentSize`  in `zstd-1.5.6-2.fc41.aarch64`

but then `ZSTD_getFrameContentSize` from `zstd-1.5.6` calls `ZSTD_getFrameHeader` in fluent-bit's `zstd-1.5.7`!

These don't have to be compatible with regard to *internal* ABI!  Maybe they are, by accident, but it's not a guarantee.

I can't trigger the segfault on Fedora. But we can definitely see the mixing of the two library versions. Where the dynamically loaded `libzstd` calls into the statically loaded one which is ripe for trouble.

Suspecting an ABI incompatibility, I tried using `fluent-bit-3.2.7` instead. This version uses `zstd-1.5.6`, the same version as in NixOS. So we wouldn't expect a crash. However, it would still segfault.

Then I noticed that the `sizeof(ZSTD_DCtx)`  from `fluent-bit` is 16 bytes bigger than the one from NixOS.  This means that when we call into `fluent-bits`'s copy of `libzstd` it is modifying memory past what has been `malloc`'d by `libsystemd`'s call to `ZSTD_createDCtx`  and thus writing out of bounds. This probably corrupts enough memory that subsequent `free()` segfaults.

Digging in further, I found the following: https://github.com/facebook/zstd/blame/dev/lib/decompress/zstd_decompress_internal.h#L183

When `ZSTD_LEGACY_SUPPORT` is set, 16 more bytes get added to the `ZSTD_DCtx` struct.

In NixOS, we're building `libzstd` with [`ZSTD_LEGACY_SUPPORT=0`](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/9d4a057b4ec7f18300fccdf64cfd94344c9536cc/pkgs/tools/compression/zstd/default.nix#L10).

Fedora and fluent-bit both use the default setting of `ZSTD_LEGACY_SUPPORT=1`.

For this reason; Fedora doesn't segfault on `free()` as no bytes are written past what is `malloc()`d.

I hope that I have demonstrated with this the issue at hand and that it has nothing to do with nix. Instead it is caused by two copies of `libzstd` being interleaved with different compiler flags leading to memory corruption.

There might be other distros that also build `libzstd` with `ZSTD_LEGACY_SUPPORT=0` and they will run into the same issues

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I just noticed the following in the zstd README:

- The C compiler macros `ZSTDLIB_VISIBLE`, `ZSTDERRORLIB_VISIBLE` and `ZDICTLIB_VISIBLE`
  can be overridden to control the visibility of zstd's API. Additionally,
  `ZSTDLIB_STATIC_API` and `ZDICTLIB_STATIC_API` can be overridden to control the visibility
  of zstd's static API. Specifically, it can be set to `ZSTDLIB_HIDDEN` to hide the symbols
  from the shared library. These macros default to `ZSTDLIB_VISIBILITY`,
  `ZSTDERRORLIB_VSIBILITY`, and `ZDICTLIB_VISIBILITY` if unset, for backwards compatibility
  with the old macro names.

which looks promising. I'll try setting these in `cmake/zstd.cmake` and see if it fixes the issue

So technically this issue is not solved. And you might run into it when you are going to deploy fluent-bit as currently packaged by you to distros when they start shipping newer systemd versions and their libzstd version or build flags goes out of sync with fluent-bit's vendored version. It's a bit of a ticking time bomb.

But for me it's solved as I am not statically linking these deps in NixOS anymore. Hence closing

I hope you'll remember this issue if you start running into crashes once Debian, Ubuntu and Fedora start shipping newer versions of systemd 

I personally don't have the bandwidth at the moment to contribute fixes to the build system so that fluent-bit doesn't export symbols of all the libraries that you vendor.
